items.title: Dundas Street East Lanes Shut After Motorcyclist Hurt in Early-Morning Mississauga Crash
items.summary: Peel Regional Police say a motorcyclist was seriously injured in a crash involving a vehicle and a motorcycle early Wednesday morning in Mississauga. According to police, the collision happened at Dundas Street East and Haines Road, and the motorcycle rider was taken to hospital with serious injuries. Police said the eastbound lanes of Dundas Street East are closed at Haines Road, with one westbound lane also shut down. Officers added that Haines Road is closed to northbound traffic south of Dundas Street East while the investigation continues. Police are advising drivers travelling through the area to expect delays until the roads reopen.

items.title: Camping-Themed CABINFEST Returns to Port Credit with Proceeds Headed to Local Food Bank
items.summary: CABIN: Barber and Gentleman Supply is bringing its annual CABINFEST back to Port Credit on Saturday, Nov. 7, with proceeds going to The Compass Food Bank. According to organizers, the one-day festival takes place at the Small Arms Inspection Building at 1352 Lakeshore Rd. and combines live music, entertainment and local vendors. This year's theme is camping, and organizers say they are encouraging attendees to show up in campy attire, including red flannel and denim. The lineup includes DJs playing old-school, funk, rock and soul hits alongside music from the 1980s, plus a silent disco. Organizers said all proceeds from the event will benefit The Compass Food Bank, located at 427 Lakeshore Rd. E.

items.title: Peel Police Say Heavy Response to UTM Dorm Standoff Aimed at Preventing 'Mass Casualty Situation'
items.summary: Peel Regional Police say a 19-year-old man wanted in an intimate-partner violence investigation in Brampton died of an apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound while barricaded inside a residence at the University of Toronto's Mississauga campus. According to police Const. Bell, who spoke to reporters Tuesday, the victim in the Brampton incident was injured and the suspect was reportedly armed with a handgun. Police said officers quickly connected the Brampton case to the man later found barricaded at the Mississauga dorm. The force said its response was deliberately heavy to prevent what officers described as the possibility of a mass casualty situation. Police said occupants of the dorm were evacuated without incident. Officers tried to make contact with the armed man after arriving, and witnesses reported hearing multiple shots soon after.

items.title: Peel Police Seek Public's Help Locating Vulnerable 32-Year-Old Man Last Seen in Mississauga
items.summary: Peel Regional Police say they are searching for Roman, a 32-year-old man considered vulnerable, who was last seen in Mississauga on Tuesday. According to police, he was last seen on foot on Bough Beeches Boulevard. Officers describe him as about five-foot-ten with a medium build and long brown hair. Police said he was last seen wearing a beige hoodie with a peace sign logo, grey track pants and grey Crocs. Investigators are asking anyone with information about Roman's whereabouts to come forward. Anyone with information is asked to call Peel Regional Police at 416-808-2222.

items.title: Mississauga Sets Nov. 21 Date for Second Year of Revived Downtown Santa Claus Parade
items.summary: The City of Mississauga says its Santa Claus parade will return to the downtown core on Saturday, Nov. 21, under the theme "Sauga's Home for the Holidays." According to the city, the parade will run alongside the lighting of the Christmas tree and the seasonal opening of the city's largest outdoor ice rink at Celebration Square. City officials said Santa's sleigh will pass through Celebration Square and light the tree to mark the start of the holiday season. The city brought the parade back to the downtown core near Square One in November 2025 after a nearly 25-year absence, calling that return a highly successful event. Officials said they expect the parade to become a signature winter tradition in the downtown area for years to come. The city said this year's event will include illuminated floats, marching bands and family-friendly entertainment.

items.title: Mississauga Library Brings Back Free Comic Expo for Two Days at Hazel McCallion Branch
items.summary: Mississauga Library says its annual Comic Expo returns for two free, drop-in days at the Hazel McCallion Central Library on Nov. 6 and 7. According to the library, Friday's programming includes board games, Dungeons & Dragons sessions, Pokemon-themed crafts, collectibles trading, superhero trivia and a movie screening. The library said Saturday is the larger of the two days, featuring more than 120 exhibitors, special guests, workshops and panels. Organizers said Saturday also includes a cosplay red carpet where attendees can dress up as their favourite comic characters, along with board game demos and video game free-play sessions. The event is open to all ages and takes place at the branch's address, 301 Burnhamthorpe Rd. The library said exhibitors and special guests appear only on the Saturday portion of the event, while Friday is geared toward games and activities.

items.title: Ward 9 Councillor Pushes for Safety Review After Student Struck by Car Near Edenwood Middle School
items.summary: Mississauga Ward 9 Councillor Martin Reid says his office is working with city staff and community partners to review road safety near Edenwood Middle School after a student was struck by a vehicle while riding a bicycle last Friday. According to Reid, the review will focus on school routes and pedestrian crossings in the area. Peel Regional Police told INSAUGA the student was struck near Edenwood Drive and Aquitaine Avenue on Friday morning. Police said the young person suffered minor injuries and did not need to go to hospital. Police added that the driver stopped at the scene and offered assistance after the collision. Reid said his thoughts are with the student and their family, and he wished them a full recovery.

items.title: Investigators Probe Seatbelt Use as Mississauga Teen Remains Hospitalized After Fatal Guelph-Area Crash
items.summary: Ontario Provincial Police say they are investigating whether a lack of seatbelts contributed to the fatal crash near Guelph that killed four teenagers over the weekend. According to the Peel District School Board, one current and two former students were among those who died when the car left Watson Road South, struck a guardrail and went into a ravine early Saturday. Police identified the dead as a 17-year-old girl from Mississauga, a 15-year-old girl from Milton and two 19-year-old men from Mississauga and Brampton. OPP said a 17-year-old girl from Mississauga remained in hospital with life-altering injuries, while a 16-year-old from Mississauga suffered non-life-threatening injuries. The school board said it is providing support to students, families and staff affected by the crash and extended condolences to the victims' families. The board said it would not comment further while the investigation continues.
